metadata.construction_scope: A dated official company-partner disclosure says the June 25 first-stone ceremony marked the start of works. A ceremony and generic start-of-works statement do not isolate site preparation, clearing, civil works, excavation, foundations, structural frame, shell, MEP, energization, commissioning, completion, occupancy, or operation.

metadata.role_scope: Cuerva calls Alto Infrastructure the digital-infrastructure developer and describes Cuerva as a strategic energy-infrastructure partner. Alto's current first-party web application describes its platform as designing, building, and operating data centers and presents 24/7 on-site operations for SP01. This supports Alto as developer and intended operator. Cuerva is retained as a partner in metadata and is not normalized as the utility. No owner, landlord, tenant, user, customer, contractor, investor, or named utility is established.
metadata.workload_scope: Cuerva explicitly identifies SP01 as specialized for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing and describes high-density compute for advanced AI models. These are intended design classifications for the future facility, not current workloads, installed hardware, utilization, or operating load. The wording does not safely separate AI training from AI inference.
metadata.power_scope: The up-to-100 MW figure is redundant electrical power required only when the project is fully built. The existing 132/66/20 kV substation and planned 220/132 kV substation describe an energy-infrastructure plan. None is normalized as Phase 1 critical IT, gross facility demand, grid-connection capacity, generation, current load, annual energy, or measured consumption.
metadata.renewable_water_scope: Future 100% renewable supply, closed-loop liquid cooling, and practically zero cooling-water language describes intended design and procurement. It creates no measured renewable share, water use, WUE, PUE, current consumption, or operating observation.
